data.name: Ferdinand
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic 'Farthag', meaning 'brave, fearless', Ferdinand is a strong name with deep roots in European history and legend. data.cultural_impact: Ferdinand has a rich cultural history, dating back to the early medieval period. The name was common among European nobility and kings, perhaps most famously the Habsburg monarch Ferdinand I, who played a significant role in the political landscape of Europe during the 16th century. Ferdinand is also the name of several saints, including Saint Ferdinand of Pamiers, a French priest and martyr who is venerated for his devotion to the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ferdinand holds deep significance in the spiritual realm, as it is associated with Saint Ferdinand, a symbol of bravery and strength in the face of adversity. In Christian tradition, the saint's life serves as an inspiring example of faith and resilience. Ferdinand's story of steadfastness and unwavering commitment to his beliefs is a reminder of the importance of courage and perseverance in the face of obstacles. Thus, the name carries a powerful spiritual message, encouraging those who bear it to draw strength from their faith and to face challenges with bravery and determination.
